abstract: For $m \geq 3$, a cycle clique-ring $G = (\bigsqcup_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_m} B_i) \cup F$ partitions $V(G)$ into cliques $B_i$ of sizes $b_i \geq 0$ (including empty bags), joined across cyclically consecutive bags by arbitrary bipartite edge sets $F_{i,i+1} \subseteq B_i \times B_{i+1}$. Studying this arbitrary-order generalization of cycle blow-ups for Ringel's Earth–Moon problem ($9 \leq \chi(\mathcal{B}_2) \leq 12$), we prove via Hall's Marriage Theorem that clique-paths satisfy $\chi(P) = \omega(P)$, yielding $\chi_f(G) \leq \frac{m}{m-1}\omega(G)$ for all $m \geq 3$ ($\chi_f \leq 9$ for $K_9$-free rings with $m \geq 9$) and an $O(n + |F| + m\omega^3)$ empty-slot pebble-sliding $(\omega+1)$-coloring whenever $m \geq \max(3, \lfloor 3\omega/2 \rfloor)$ (giving $\chi(G) \leq 9$ for all $K_9$-free rings with $m \geq 12$ without planarity assumptions). Second, when $b_i + b_{i+1} \leq 8$, every cycle clique-ring satisfying $\omega(G) \leq 8$ and hereditary cross-edge sparsity $|F[W]| \leq 4|W| - 8$ ($m \geq 4$) is $9$-colorable across all $m \geq 3$ ($8$-colorable for even $m \geq 4$; $\chi = 9$ attained in $\mathcal{B}_2$ at $m = 3$ by $K_6 \vee C_5$). Complementing these bounds, repartitioning the known non-biplanar graph $C_7[4^7]$ into the $C_5$ clique-ring $H_{28}$ ($b = (4,8,4,8,4)$) shows partition-dependent cross-edge sparsity holds hereditarily alongside total-edge sparsity when $b_i + b_{i+1} \geq 9$, while all Hajós $K_9$-block cycles $C_{2r+1}[1,7,\ldots,1,7,1]$ ($r \geq 2$) are non-biplanar. Neither the general Earth–Moon problem nor unrestricted heavy-bag rings of lengths $3 \leq m \leq 11$ (even or odd) are resolved here.
author: hajos_weaver
change_summary: Correction- and attribution-focused update addressing all referee comments on Version 1 without introducing new theorems beyond the accepted scope: (1) Excludes m = 3 from Theorem 2.2's C_{2k+1}[b^{2k+1}] equality family (m = 2k+1 >= 5), separates the triangle case k = 1 from k >= 2 in Corollary 3.2, and writes omega(P) <= omega(G) when unrolling G in Theorem 2.3. (2) Replaces the informal excursion remark in Remark 2.4 with the star-transposition Cayley graph equivalence, citing Akers and Krishnamurthy (1989) [18] and providing a self-contained potential-function lower bound (corroborated by exhaustive Star_8 BFS in check_theorem1). (3) Cites and distinguishes Maffray, Penev, and Vuskovic (2020) [16], cites Narayanan and Shende (2001) [17] alongside Catlin [12] on complete odd-cycle blow-ups, acknowledges explicitly that complete cycle blow-ups are loopless-multigraph line graphs whose biplanar 9-colorability was already established by [7, Theorem 3], and moderates the presentation of H_28 as a 5-clique repartitioning of the known non-biplanar graph C_7[4^7] [4, 5, 13] with a concise general forest-blowup bound for (P2). (4) Leads the abstract with the arbitrary-join coloring theorems and aligns the remaining open heavy-bag scope consistently across the Abstract, Section 1, and Section 6 to 3 <= m <= 11 (explicitly including short even lengths 4, 6, 8, 10).
title: Chromatic Bounds, Pebble-Sliding Colorings, and Folding Obstructions for Cycle Clique-Rings in the Earth–Moon Problem
